question: q-125457

original_content.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{1}{y}\,i-\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
original_content.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{y}\,i-\frac{1}{x}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-1-1 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(-2)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-2(2\pi )-0 \\  & =-4\pi \end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{1}{y}\,i-\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ Interpret circulation as the sum of four convergent improper line integrals over the open quadrant arcs, with independent one-sided limits at $(\pm1,0)$ and $(0,\pm1)$. The field is undefined at those four points, so the original ordinary circulation is not defined.
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The original field is undefined at the four axis intersections, so an ordinary line integral over the whole circle is not defined. For the explicit improper interpretation, $r(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ traverses the unit circle counterclockwise. On each open quadrant arc,

$$\frac{1}{y}\,dx=\frac{-\sin t}{\sin t}\,dt=-dt,\qquad-\frac{1}{x}\,dy=\frac{-\cos t}{\cos t}\,dt=-dt.$$

Thus the scalar pullback is $-2$. Each endpoint has the finite one-sided limit $-2$, so each open-arc integral converges absolutely and equals $-\pi$. Their sum is $\Gamma_{\mathrm{imp}}=-4\pi$, the unchanged option a. No principal-value cancellation is used, and $F$ remains undefined at the excluded points.

rationale: Supply the omitted convergent improper-integral convention. Four independently convergent quadrant integrals yield -4pi; ordinary original circulation remains undefined.
